decisions.rationale: Mega Charizard Y is the cornerstone, activating Drought turn-one to boost Fire attacks and weaken Water threats. Torkoal pairs as a bulky sun setter and Eruption nuke, while Arbok provides Intimidate to soften physical attackers like Garchomp and Blaziken. Victreebel in the back leverages Chlorophyll under sun for late-game sweep pressure with Solar Beam and Sludge Bomb. This lead maximizes early sun control and defensive utility while preserving sweepers for endgame.
decisions.notebook: Primary win condition: Drought + Chlorophyll sweep with Mega Charizard Y and Victreebel. Sun weakens Water types (Rotom-Wash, Starmie) and boosts Fire attacks, while Chlorophyll outspeeds and pressures with Grass/Poison coverage. Arbok’s Intimidate and Glare disrupt physical threats (Garchomp, Blaziken), and Toxapex provides Toxic Spikes and Haze utility. Volcarona is a late-game Quiver Dance sweeper under sun. Prioritize preserving Mega Charizard Y and Victreebel for endgame, using Torkoal and Arbok as early-game pivots. Watch for opponent’s Protect stalling and Thunder Wave speed control; plan to outspeed with Chlorophyll or disrupt with Glare.

decisions.rationale: Garchomp outspeeds Mega Charizard Y (169 vs 120-152) and OHKOes with Rock Slide. Starmie outspeeds Volcarona (183 vs 132-167) and Ice Beams it. Archaludon and Rotom-Wash provide bulk, status, and secondary Rock Slide for cleanup.
decisions.notebook: Opponent runs double Drought (Mega Charizard Y + Torkoal) sun with fast Fire/Bug threats. Rock Slide from Garchomp and Archaludon 4x OHKOes Charizard Y and Volcarona. Starmie outspeeds sun core and Ice Beams Volcarona. Blaziken Speed Boosts behind sun-boosted Flare Blitz to clean. Rotom-Wash burns physical attackers. Garchomp Jolly 169 Speed outspeeds Mega Charizard Y max 152. Starmie Timid 183 Speed outspeeds Volcarona max 167. Chlorophyll Victreebel reaches 180-244 Speed in sun, outspeeds Starmie at max. Plan: Lead Garchomp + Starmie to handle sun core turn 1. Bring Archaludon for bulk and Thunder Wave. Rotom-Wash for Will-O-Wisp on physical threats. Blaziken as endgame sweeper if sun is controlled.

decisions.rationale: Mega Evolving Charizard immediately secures Drought permanently, enabling sun-boosted Fire attacks and weakening Water-type threats. Heat Wave + Eruption under sun pressures both foes, risking OHKOs or heavy damage before they can retaliate. Protect variants are safer but delay pressure and let foes chip Charizard. Rock Slide and Thunderbolt are the biggest threats, but sun-boosted Fire damage mitigates them by threatening OHKOs first.
decisions.notebook: Primary win condition remains Drought + Chlorophyll sweep with Mega Charizard Y and Victreebel. Mega Evolving Charizard Y on Turn 1 is critical to secure permanent sun, weaken Water-type threats (Starmie, Rotom-Wash), and enable sun-boosted Fire attacks. Torkoal’s Eruption under sun is a high-damage opener, but Protect may be necessary if opponent’s lead is overly aggressive. Arbok’s Intimidate and Glare are key to disrupt physical threats like Garchomp and Blaziken. Victreebel should be preserved for late-game Chlorophyll sweep, avoiding early exposure to Ice Beam or Thunderbolt. Watch for opponent’s Protect stalling and Thunder Wave; plan to outspeed with Chlorophyll or disrupt with Glare. Rotom-Wash and Starmie are priority targets for Victreebel’s Solar Beam and Sludge Bomb under sun.

decisions.rationale: Both my mons outspeed the sun core. Rock Slide (4x Charizard, 2x Torkoal) + Hydro Pump (2x Charizard) = guaranteed KO on Charizard before it Mega Evolves and Solar Beams Starmie. Even if Hydro Pump misses (80%), Rock Slide alone minimum 78.4% and likely OHKOes. Removes the biggest threat immediately while spreading damage to Torkoal.

Garchomp Rock Slide OHKOs Charizard-Mega-Y if unprotected. Starmie Hydro Pump also threatens OHKO. Protect on Charizard-Mega-Y avoids both risks while preserving sun. Torkoal Protect preserves Eruption PP for later and avoids Earthquake or Rock Slide. This line minimizes risk while maintaining offensive pressure.
decisions.notebook: Garchomp is confirmed Jolly with Life Orb and Rough Skin; Rock Slide is a guaranteed OHKO on Charizard-Mega-Y. Starmie is Timid with Wise Glasses; Hydro Pump can OHKO Charizard-Mega-Y under optimal conditions. Starmie’s Thunderbolt is a secondary threat but not an OHKO. Preserve Charizard-Mega-Y as the primary sun setter and sweeper. Torkoal’s Eruption is powerful but should not be wasted if opponent Protects or switches. Arbok’s Intimidate and Glare are critical for disrupting physical threats like Garchomp and Blaziken. Victreebel remains the late-game Chlorophyll sweeper; avoid early exposure to Ice Beam or Thunderbolt. Watch for opponent’s Protect stalling and Thunder Wave; plan to outspeed with Chlorophyll or disrupt with Glare. Rotom-Wash and Starmie are priority targets for Victreebel’s Solar Beam and Sludge Bomb under sun.

decisions.rationale: Starmie at 17% is likely dead anyway to Solar Beam or Earth Power. Sacrificing it to KO Charizard (4x Rock Slide + 2x Hydro Pump) removes the biggest threat and breaks the sun core. Rock Slide spread also pressures Torkoal 2x if Charizard Protects. Garchomp at 30% survives most neutral hits and can clean up next turn.

Rotom-Wash for Will-O-Wisp on physical threats. Blaziken as endgame sweeper if sun is controlled.

Torkoal Eruption OHKO on Starmie and heavy damage on Garchomp maximizes damage output under sun. Protect or switching risks losing Charizard-Mega-Y to Rock Slide or Hydro Pump.

decisions.rationale: Arbok’s Intimidate softens Garchomp’s Rock Slide/Earthquake, Glare disrupts Starmie/Blaziken, and Victreebel outspeeds under sun to OHKO Starmie with Solar Beam. Double Victreebel risks both being KOed by Rock Slide.
decisions.notebook: Victreebel’s Solar Beam under sun is a guaranteed OHKO on Starmie (122 Speed outspeeds Starmie’s 148-183). Arbok’s Intimidate reduces Garchomp’s Attack, mitigating Rock Slide/Earthquake damage. Glare cripples fast threats like Starmie or Blaziken. Prioritize eliminating Starmie first to prevent Hydro Pump or Thunderbolt pressure. Watch for opponent’s Protect stalling and Thunder Wave; use Glare to disrupt. Rotom-Wash and Archaludon are secondary targets for Victreebel’s Sludge Bomb. Blaziken’s Speed Boost is a late-game threat; preserve Arbok’s Glare for it.

decisions.rationale: Garchomp Rock Slide guarantees KO on Charizard-Mega-Y at 49% HP (78-178% damage). Starmie Hydro Pump into Torkoal has 80-190% damage range for possible OHKO at 62% HP. Both my Pokémon outspeed the sun core, so we attack first. Removing both threats is critical since Starmie at 17% dies to any Torkoal hit. Hydro Pump's 80% accuracy is acceptable given the high damage potential and Charizard's guaranteed removal.
decisions.notebook: Double Drought sun core (Mega Charizard Y + Torkoal with Heat Rock) extends sun to 6+ turns. Garchomp Jolly 169 Speed outspeeds Mega Charizard Y max 152. Starmie Timid 183 Speed outspeeds Volcarona max 167. Rock Slide 4x OHKOes Charizard Y and Volcarona. Starmie Hydro Pump OHKOes Torkoal and Charizard Y. Chlorophyll Victreebel reaches 180-244 Speed in sun, outspeeds Starmie at max. Opponent tends to Protect on turn after taking heavy damage. Plan: Lead Garchomp + Starmie to break sun core turn 1. Bring Archaludon for bulk and Thunder Wave support. Rotom-Wash for Will-O-Wisp on physical threats. Control sun to enable endgame sweepers.

decisions.rationale: Starmie is the highest threat due to Hydro Pump/Thunderbolt. Solar Beam OHKO under sun is guaranteed. Sucker Punch ensures Starmie dies even if it tries to attack. Glare is redundant if Starmie is KOed. Protect is unnecessary with Garchomp at 20% and Starmie dead.
decisions.notebook: Victreebel’s Solar Beam under sun OHKOes Starmie (122 Speed outspeeds Starmie’s 148-183). Arbok’s Sucker Punch ensures Starmie dies if it attempts to attack. Prioritize eliminating Starmie to remove Hydro Pump/Thunderbolt pressure. Glare is reserved for Blaziken or Rotom-Wash later. Garchomp at 20% is manageable with Intimidate and Victreebel’s resistance to Rock Slide. Watch for opponent’s Protect stalling and Thunder Wave; use Glare to disrupt fast threats.

decisions.rationale: Both Pokémon are at critical HP and outsped by Chlorophyll Victreebel. Archaludon resists Solar Beam and Sludge Bomb (0.5x each), takes neutral Sucker Punch, and gains Stamina boosts from physical hits. Starmie Protects to survive. This resets the board with a bulky switch-in while preserving Starmie for later.

Turn 4: Arbok (Intimidate, Expert Belt) and Victreebel (Chlorophyll, Victreebelite) entered. Both my Pokémon at critical HP. Bringing Archaludon to resist Grass/Poison and pivot.

decisions.rationale: Starmie is the immediate Hydro Pump/Thunderbolt threat. Victreebel’s Solar Beam OHKOes Starmie under sun, and Arbok’s Sucker Punch ensures Starmie dies if it attacks. This line removes Starmie before it can retaliate or spread status, maximizing win probability.
decisions.notebook: Victreebel’s Solar Beam under sun OHKOes Starmie (122 Speed outspeeds Starmie’s 148–183). Arbok’s Sucker Punch guarantees Starmie’s KO if it attempts to attack. Prioritize eliminating Starmie to remove Hydro Pump/Thunderbolt pressure. Glare is reserved for Blaziken or Rotom-Wash later. Garchomp at 20% is manageable with Intimidate and Victreebel’s resistance to Rock Slide. Watch for opponent’s Protect stalling and Thunder Wave; use Glare to disrupt fast threats.

decisions.rationale: Victreebel in sun outspeeds Starmie ~94% and will Solar Beam it for KO. Starmie at 17% is nearly dead anyway. Thunder Wave from safe Archaludon paralyzes their win condition, and Ice Beam chips if Starmie somehow moves first or Victreebel targets Archaludon. Maximizes chance to cripple Victreebel while accepting Starmie's likely loss.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Sun core (Mega Charizard Y + Torkoal Heat Rock) broken turn 3. Arbok (Intimidate, Expert Belt, Jolly 110-145) and Victreebel (Chlorophyll, Victreebelite, Modest 180-244 sun) remain. Victreebel outspeeds Starmie 94% in sun. Archaludon (Adamant, Stamina, Leftovers) immune to Poison, 0.25x Grass, safe pivot. Rotom-Wash (Levitate, Sitrus Berry) bulky Water pivot with Will-O-Wisp for physical threats. Garchomp (Jolly, Life Orb, Rough Skin, 21%) fragile but fast endgame sweeper if sun controlled. Plan: paralyze Victreebel, burn Arbok with Rotom-Wash, sweep with Archaludon or Garchomp. Opponent Protects after heavy damage.

decisions.rationale: Rotom-Wash is the safe pivot: 100% HP, Levitate, resists Poison, burns Arbok with Will-O-Wisp, and Hydro Pumps Victreebel SE. Garchomp at 21% HP with Life Orb recoil cannot survive taking hits. Archaludon passes to maintain Def +1 and pressure.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Sun core broken T3. Opponent: Arbok (Intimidate, Expert Belt, Jolly, par) + Victreebel (Chlorophyll, Victreebelite, Modest). Plan: Rotom-Wash burns Arbok, Archaludon tanks Grass/Poison, sweep with Archaludon or Garchomp. Opponent Protects after heavy damage. Victreebel outspeeds in sun. Archaludon immune to Poison, 0.25x Grass, Def +1 from Stamina. Garchomp 21% HP fragile endgame sweeper.

decisions.rationale: Rotom-Wash is the immediate Hydro Pump threat. Sucker Punch (priority +1) guarantees KO if Rotom-Wash attacks. Solar Beam under sun OHKOes or nearly OHKOes Rotom-Wash, removing the Water-type threat. Protect/Glare is safer but lets Rotom-Wash survive to Hydro Pump next turn. Coil is too slow against fast threats.
decisions.notebook: Victreebel’s Solar Beam under sun OHKOes Starmie (confirmed) and nearly OHKOes Rotom-Wash (82-184%). Arbok’s Sucker Punch guarantees KO on any attacking Rotom-Wash. Prioritize eliminating Rotom-Wash to remove Hydro Pump pressure. Glare is reserved for Blaziken or fast threats later. Garchomp at 20% is manageable with Intimidate and resistances. Watch for opponent’s Protect stalling and Thunder Wave; use Glare to disrupt fast threats if needed.

decisions.rationale: Flash Cannon pressures Victreebel (neutral hit) while Will-O-Wisp burns Arbok, halving its physical damage. Rotom-Wash's Sitrus Berry + 144 SpD should survive Solar Beam. Burning paralyzed Arbok further neutalizes its threat. Aggressive play maintains momentum.

Plan: Rotom-Wash burns Arbok, Archaludon tanks Grass/Poison, sweep with Archaludon or Garchomp. Opponent Protects after heavy damage. Victreebel outspeeds in sun. Burn + paralyze on Arbok severely limits its offensive output.

decisions.rationale: Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Protect stalls for sun turns, blocks spread Earthquake/Fire Fang, and forces opponent to reveal next move. Preserves Arbok and Victreebel from immediate KO risk while maintaining offensive pressure afterward.
decisions.notebook: Victreebel’s Solar Beam under sun is a nuke but requires Protect support to avoid being double-targeted. Arbok’s Coil is strong but risky under Earthquake/Fire Fang pressure. Glare is reserved for Blaziken or fast threats later. Prioritize sun management and Protect stalling to force opponent into unfavorable positions. Garchomp at 20% is manageable with Intimidate and resistances, but spread moves are lethal. Watch for Thunder Wave disrupting Arbok’s speed.

decisions.rationale: Focus fire on Victreebel (56% HP). Flash Cannon (24-56%) + Fire Fang (38-90%) = 62-146% combined, guaranteed KO if both hit. Victreebel moves first and likely KOs Garchomp with Solar Beam, but if it uses Sludge Bomb (8-30%), Garchomp survives and we KO Victreebel. Even if Garchomp dies, Flash Cannon leaves Victreebel at 0-32% for Archaludon to clean up next turn.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Sun core broken T3. Opponent: Arbok (Intimidate, Expert Belt, Jolly, par) + Victreebel (Chlorophyll, Victreebelite, Modest). Victreebel outspeeds in sun, Solar Beam KOs low-HP targets. Archaludon tanks Grass/Poison (immune/0.25x), Def +1 from Stamina. Garchomp fragile endgame sweeper at 21% HP. Plan: Focus Victreebel with super-effective Fire Fang + Flash Cannon. Arbok paralyzed and less threatening. Archaludon clean up remaining foes.

decisions.rationale: Sun ends turn 9. Garchomp at 20% is OHKOed by Solar Beam under sun. Protect stalls sun, avoids Earthquake/Fire Fang double target. Coil risks OHKO from Earthquake. Glare is redundant vs paralyzed Garchomp. Solar Beam on Garchomp secures KO and sun management.
decisions.notebook: Victreebel’s Solar Beam under sun is a nuke but requires Protect support to avoid being double-targeted. Arbok’s Coil is strong but risky under Earthquake pressure. Prioritize sun management and Protect stalling to force opponent into unfavorable positions. Garchomp at low HP is a priority KO target. Archaludon’s Thunder Wave is disruptive but less urgent than sun expiry. Mega Victreebel’s Innards Out is a late-game cleanup tool if sun is secured.

decisions.rationale: Victreebel moves first in sun and can KO 21% Garchomp with Solar Beam (2x). Archaludon Flash Cannon pressures Victreebel while Garchomp Protect preserves our endgame sweeper. Archaludon tanks Grass/Poison (immune/0.25x) and has Def +1, so it's safe to attack. This keeps Garchomp alive to clean up after sun fades.

Garchomp at 20% is priority KO. Coil avoids Earthquake spread damage, Protect stalls sun for one more turn. If Garchomp stays in, Solar Beam next turn OHKOs. If Archaludon Protects, Victreebel survives Flash Cannon and can nuke next turn. Minimizes risk of double target.

Arbok’s Coil is strong but risky under Earthquake pressure; prioritize sun management and Protect stalling to force opponent into unfavorable positions. Garchomp at low HP is a priority KO target. Mega Victreebel’s Innards Out is a late-game cleanup tool if sun is secured. Archaludon’s Thunder Wave is disruptive but less urgent than sun expiry or Garchomp KO.

Protecting Garchomp keeps it alive while Archaludon cleans up. If Victreebel Megas into Innards Out, Archaludon takes only ~12% recoil and survives to clean paralyzed Arbok.

Victreebel outspeeds Archaludon base, Solar Beam KOs low-HP targets. Archaludon tanks Grass/Poison (immune/0.25x), Def +1 from Stamina. Garchomp fragile endgame at low HP. Plan: Archaludon clean up with Flash Cannon/Rock Slide. Arbok paralyzed, less threatening. If Victreebel Megas, Innards Out punishes contact KOs on low-HP Garchomp; use Archaludon special moves to avoid recoil. Archaludon 100% HP, Def +1, Leftovers vs Arbok 100% par is winning matchup.

Prioritize sun management and Protect stalling to force opponent into unfavorable positions. Mega Victreebel’s Innards Out is a late-game cleanup tool if sun is secured and threats are weakened. Garchomp at 21% must Protect vs Arbok's priority Sucker Punch. Archaludon at 100% with Def+1 comfortably tanks any Innards Out recoil (~12% max HP) and cleans up Arbok next turn.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Sun core broken T3. Opponent: Arbok (Intimidate, Expert Belt, Jolly, par, Coil boosts) + Victreebel (Chlorophyll/Victreebelite, Modest). Archaludon tanks Grass/Poison (immune/0.25x), Stamina stacks Def. Garchomp fragile endgame. Plan: Archaludon cleanup with Flash Cannon/Rock Slide; avoid contact on Mega Victreebel to dodge Innards Out. Arbok paralyzed, less threatening. Archaludon 100% HP Def+1 Leftovers vs par Arbok is winning matchup. Cross-game: vs sun teams, break sun early with Rotom/Starmie; Archaludon is primary win-con vs Grass/Poison cores; Garchomp is finisher but preserve HP.

decisions.rationale: Garchomp is 20% HP and paralyzed, making Sucker Punch a near-certain KO. Removing it eliminates Earthquake and Rock Slide threats, simplifying the endgame. Protect/Flash Cannon from foes is less urgent than this KO. Coil is too slow; Poison Jab lacks priority.
decisions.notebook: Prioritize Sucker Punch on low-HP Garchomp to eliminate Earthquake threat. Sun management remains critical for Victreebel’s Solar Beam, but immediate KOs take precedence. Archaludon’s Thunder Wave is disruptive but less urgent than removing Garchomp. Innards Out on Mega Victreebel is a late-game cleanup tool if sun is secured and threats are weakened. Always account for paralysis halving Arbok’s Speed.

decisions.rationale: Flash Cannon + Earthquake deals 116-279% combined damage, likely KOing Arbok. If Arbok Sucker Punches Garchomp, Garchomp dies but Archaludon's Flash Cannon still hits, and Archaludon wins the 1v1 (Flash Cannon 25-59% vs Arbok's Sucker Punch 18-21% on Archaludon). Protecting Garchomp lets Arbok survive unnecessarily, dragging the game and risking paralysis or bad rolls.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: vs sun cores, break sun early with Rotom/Starmie. Archaludon is primary win-con vs Grass/Poison, tanks with Stamina. Garchomp is fragile finisher, preserve HP. Cross-game: vs priority users (Sucker Punch), protect fragile Pokémon or go for KO before they act. Archaludon 1v1 vs physical attackers is winning matchup due to Def boosts and Leftovers. Paralyzed foes are less threatening but priority moves bypass speed.

decisions.rationale: Sucker Punch (priority +1) is the only way to outspeed and KO Archaludon before it can use Rock Slide or Flash Cannon, eliminating the immediate spread threat. Coil and Glare are too slow and risk letting Archaludon KO Arbok first.
decisions.notebook: Archaludon’s Rock Slide is a lethal spread move that must be prioritized over status or stat boosts. Sucker Punch is the only reliable tool to outspeed and remove it. Innards Out on Mega Victreebel remains a late-game cleanup option if sun is secured and threats are weakened. Always account for paralysis halving Arbok’s Speed and prioritize eliminating Earthquake/Garchomp-level threats first.

decisions.rationale: Flash Cannon targets Arbok's -1 SpD and likely KOs from 37% HP. Sucker Punch hits first with priority but only does max 18.8% to Archaludon's +1 Def, so Archaludon survives and fires Flash Cannon. Even if Arbok survives the Flash Cannon, it's at ~12% HP and Archaludon wins next turn. Protect wastes momentum and lets Arbok Coil further.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: vs sun cores, break sun early with Rotom/Starmie. Archaludon is primary win-con vs Grass/Poison, tanks with Stamina. Garchomp is fragile finisher, preserve HP. Cross-game: vs priority users (Sucker Punch), protect fragile Pokémon or go for KO before they act. Archaludon 1v1 vs physical attackers is winning matchup due to Def boosts and Leftovers. Paralyzed foes are less threatening but priority moves bypass speed. Flash Cannon is Archaludon's best STAB for hitting special-weak targets.

reflections.summary: Lost due to team-preview mismatch: Mega Victreebel and Arbok were outclassed by Archaludon's bulk, Stamina, and Flash Cannon spam, while the opponent's Garchomp and Rotom-Wash pressured sun-dependent sweepers. The lack of a counter to Archaludon's +2 Defense and consistent damage left no wincon after sun faded.
reflections.adjustment: Replace Arbok with a faster, bulkier threat (e.g., Scarf Landorus-T) to outspeed and OHKO Archaludon before it accumulates Stamina boosts. Re-evaluate Mega Victreebel's role if sun cannot be maintained against this opponent's anti-sun techs.
reflections.notebook: Opponent tendencies: 1) Archaludon prioritizes Flash Cannon spam over Rock Slide, leveraging Stamina to wall physical attackers. 2) Garchomp is a lead with Rock Slide/Earthquake coverage and Fire Fang for sun teams. 3) Rotom-Wash and Starmie are used to disrupt sun and threaten Torkoal. 4) Blaziken and Tinkaton remain unshown but may pressure Charizard-Y. Future plans: Test Archaludon's Rock Slide consistency (only used 3/12 turns) and prepare for potential Blaziken lead in Game 2. Avoid bringing Mega Victreebel if sun cannot be guaranteed.

reflections.summary: Archaludon's Stamina boosts and Leftovers recovery allowed it to outlast Arbok's physical priority and chip down Victreebel, capitalizing on the opponent's passive Protect stalling to secure the win.
reflections.adjustment: Avoid bringing both Starmie and Rotom-Wash to sun teams as they overlap in role and share a severe Solar Beam weakness; bring Toxapex instead to reliably wall Victreebel and safely pivot into physical attackers.
reflections.notebook: Opponent uses Torkoal/Charizard-Y sun with Victreebel abuser and Arbok priority support. Victreebel stalls heavily with Protect. Archaludon easily wins 1v1 physical matchups via Stamina and Leftovers. Garchomp is too fragile to priority and paralysis. Future plan: Bring Toxapex instead of dual water (Rotom/Starmie) to wall Victreebel's Solar Beam. Use Archaludon as the primary physical check.
